distractors.reason: 'Sensitive' means easily affected or emotionally delicate. It does not mean reasonable, so 'sensitive decision' sounds wrong for a sensible choice.
'Sensory' relates to the five senses (sensory input, sensory organs). It has nothing to do with good judgement.
'Sensual' refers to physical pleasure or enjoyment of the body. It is never used to describe a decision.

example_sentence: It was a ___ decision to wait for more data.
l1_interference: Falantes de português costumam traduzir 'sensível' como 'sensible', mas em inglês 'sensible' significa sensato. A palavra que corresponde a 'sensível' é 'sensitive'.
explanation: 'Sensible' describes something reasonable, practical and showing good judgement. It is a false friend for Portuguese speakers, who may expect it to mean 'sensitive'.

related_collocations.example: Saving money was a sensible choice.
Salary is a sensitive issue in many companies.
The museum offers a rich sensory experience.

memory_tip: SENSIBLE = reasonable, practical (sensible decision) | SENSITIVE = delicate, easily affected (sensitive issue, sensitive skin)
